source.title: INTRYGUE: Induction-Aware Entropy Gating for Reliable RAG Uncertainty Estimation
source.authors: A. Kuleshova; Andrei Volodichev; Daria Kotova; A. Zaytsev

page_placements.theme: Downstream readers of induction heads: entropy neurons and repetition neurons

record.tranche_reason: Extends induction-head analysis to RAG generation in open-source LLMs, measuring head ablations and induction-related activity against groundedness and entropy outcomes.
record.gate_note: The paper tests induction-head activity and causal effects in RAG settings. It does not measure training trajectories or token-index in-context-learning gains. Benchmark results for INTRYGUE itself are not rows because they report the proposed detector's performance, not induction-head behaviour. Prior results attributed to cited work are also excluded.
record.test_reason: The study uses induction heads as a tool for RAG hallucination detection. It picks the top-5 heads by induction score on repeated random sequences but reports no scores. It never tests previous-token composition, formation during training, token-index in-context learning, or prevalence across families. Its own results concern a related construct: how induction-head activity relates to groundedness, entropy and entropy neurons in 4B–13B chat models. These go under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors say induction heads support correct RAG answers and lower entropy, but also co-activate entropy neurons that push entropy up. This makes raw entropy unreliable, and gating entropy by induction activity (INTRYGUE) improves hallucination detection.
record.recipe_differences: Uses induction scores to identify heads and mean ablation to test their effects, but studies RAG groundedness and entropy rather than induction-head formation during training or the original in-context-learning loss measure.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported induction-related discrimination varies across RAG settings (AUROC 0.67–0.73). The paper also says induction signals can be weaker for short, reasoning-heavy CoQA answers, but does not report that as a direct induction-head formation or in-context-learning test.

fits_no_version.finding: Mean-ablating the top-5 induction heads raised NLL and entropy on correct CoQA answers more than random-head ablation did. This held in four 4B–8B LLMs and was robust to 1–6 heads (Fig. 9).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Induction heads causally support context-grounded answers and lower predictive entropy in RAG generation by mid-size LLMs.

fits_no_version.finding: Induction-head activity correlates with activation of final-layer entropy neurons. Ablating induction heads lowers entropy-neuron norms, with a negative median in three models; the random-head median stays near zero.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Induction heads co-activate entropy neurons outside synthetic repetition settings, including RAG decoding.

fits_no_version.finding: Induction-head SinkRate is higher for hallucinated than for grounded RAG responses (AUROC 0.67–0.73, p<1e-4, four settings).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Induction-head deactivation signals context-grounding failure (hallucination) in RAG.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The causal ablation evidence is reported mainly as figure results without numeric effect sizes in the text. The induction-head experiments are in RAG settings and do not test training-time formation or the canonical previous-token-head composition directly.

untested.parts: No previous-token-head composition and no small attention-only models. No direct [A][B]…[A]→[B] measurement is reported beyond head selection.
No token-index in-context-learning loss measure and no share of in-context learning attributed to induction heads.
Induction scores across models are not reported; heads are only selected by top score.
Training data and setup are not varied.
Few-shot task learning is not studied.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V1 and V4 'supports' labels are removed. The rows measure RAG uncertainty and entropy-neuron effects in 4B–13B chat models, not induction-head mechanism, formation or prevalence. INTRYGUE benchmark AUROCs are correctly excluded. CoQA yes/no answers are noted as having weaker induction signals.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test composition with an earlier previous-token head or directly measure [A][B] … [A] → [B] completion in its RAG experiments; its causal tests concern RAG answers and entropy.
No training-time formation window, loss-curve bump, or synchronized in-context-learning gain is measured.
No token-index in-context-learning measure or estimate of the share of large-model in-context learning carried by induction heads is reported.
The paper tests induction-related activity in a limited set of RAG model–dataset settings, not across training runs, other architectures, or modalities.
The experiments do not vary training data or setup to test when heads form or whether in-context learning persists.
Few-shot task learning and alternative mechanisms carrying it are not tested.
The paper does not study the timing or sequence of transitions during training.

relation.reason: Selects heads by induction score and studies their downstream effects, but reports no induction-score results or measurements of the catalog's claim versions.

tranche.reason: Uses induction-head identification and activity as tools for RAG uncertainty estimation. Its correlations and ablations concern entropy neurons and grounded answering, without testing V1–V7.

source_check.notes: Lower SinkRate denotes stronger induction-head activity. Figure 5a's negative medians are stated qualitatively; exact median values are not supplied. The authors' conclusion is accurately paraphrased.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: RAG response ablations and entropy-neuron measurements
reader_labels.reason: Induction-head ablation increased NLL and entropy relative to random-head ablation, and reduced entropy-neuron activation norms; this supports a causal contribution in the tested RAG setting, not the specific previous-token-head composition account (R1, R2, R5, R6, R7).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Induction-related SinkRate distinguished grounded from hallucinated responses in all four reported settings, with AUROC 0.67–0.73 (R4).
